titulo: brew and let: what can't be reassigned
tema: brew can't be assigned again; let can. Commenting with // switches a line off.

charla.texto: Lesson six: what can't be reassigned. brew keeps a value forever. If you want to change it later, use let.
If you try to reassign a brew, Coffee stops you: TypeError. It's one of the few errors that protects something.
Like an oath. What is sworn with brew is never broken. What is said with let… is negotiable.
class rule: don't occupy a space that's already occupied. it doesn't matter if a government claims it, or an army, or the great engineer himself with his holy book in hand.
and if you try to take it by force, the system throws an error. or it should. at least the compiler is consistent
…That's exactly what brew does. I'm not sure we're talking about Coffee.
of course we're talking about coffee, jair. what else would it be
Speaking of occupied spaces: Rikka's desk is completely occupied by her butt. And that definitely can't be reassigned.
My desk is occupied by me, all of me, with my notes. Focus on the exercise.

lineas: // Lesson 6: brew and let. Fill in the blanks.
[[1]] tazas = 1; // the coffee counter changes (a lot)
[[3]] escritorio = 'mine now'; // ← this can't run: switch it off
// Expected output: taken by Rikka / cups: 2
brew x = 1;  x = 2;  -> TypeError: x is already taken (brew can't be reassigned).
let  y = 1;  y = 2;  -> fine: let can change.
y = y + 1;           -> adds 1 to what it already had.
// at the start of a line turns it into a comment: it doesn't run.
Use brew by default. let only for what really changes (cups of coffee, for example).

1.error: “{valor}” won't let the value change later. The cups will change: declare them with let.

2.error: “{valor}” doesn't add another cup. To add: tazas + 1.

3.error: TypeError: “escritorio” is already taken (it's brew); with “{valor}” in front it still tries to take it. Nothing gets reassigned by force: switch that line off with //.

exito: ✔ Compiled. The desk still belongs to whoever was already there. The compiler, saner than most.

respuesta.texto: You can turn off my line, princess, but I'm still in your head. That one can't be commented out.

Jair: TypeError: Assignment to constant variable. The most honest error in the industry.
Commenting out code that doesn't work: half my career.
